mainTopic: Carrying a coal pan of ashes on שבת (from אביי's incense and גרף של רעי answers to רבא's answer about useful ashes), then reassembling a weaver's frame on שבת
overview: This עמוד opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: a lamp that was burning when שבת began became a בסיס לדבר האסור, so it may not be moved. Then רבי רומנוס reports that רבי allowed him to carry a coal pan with its ashes. רבי זירא challenges this, because רבי יוחנן allows carrying a basket with a stone only when it also holds fruit. רבי אסי answers that the pan held bits of incense, but אביי rejects this: such bits mean nothing in רבי's wealthy home. אביי then compares the pan to a גרף של רעי, and רבא rejects that comparison for two reasons. רבא gives his own answer: the ashes are useful, so the pan may be carried for their sake, and broken wood on it does not matter. A challenge from wick fragments in a lamp is answered by אביי: that ruling reflects the גליל, where oil is cheap. Finally, a new topic begins about reassembling a weaver's frame on שבת. Two rabbis permit it, רב יהודה quotes רב and שמואל that it is liable to a חטאת, and the גמרא answers that the lenient rabbis follow a different תנא, whose ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The burning lamp stays forbidden because it was a base for the flame
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up the earlier discussion. A lamp, its oil, and its wick may not be moved, because they became a base for a forbidden thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Put aside the lamp, the oil, and the wick, since it became a base for a forbidden thing.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the discussion that came on the previous עמוד. It says a lamp that was burning when שבת began may not be moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flame itself is forbidden to move. At the start of שבת, the lamp, oil, and wick were holding up that flame, so they became a בסיס לדבר האסור. Because of that, even רבי שמעון, who is usually lenient about מוקצה, agrees that this lamp may not be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Put aside, leave it. Here it means: this case is different.
A base for a forbidden thing. An object holding something that is מוקצה becomes forbidden to move as well.
Wick
Since, because

steps.whatToRemember: An object that holds up a forbidden thing (like a flame) at the start of שבת takes on that forbidden status. It becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the conclusion of the discussion on the previous עמוד. The new topic starts in the next step.

phrases.english: Leave aside the lamp, the oil, and the wick,
since it became a base for a forbidden thing.
phrases.notes: The forbidden thing is the flame that was burning when שבת began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous עמוד about moving a lamp on שבת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A lamp that was burning when שבת began may not be moved, even according to רבי שמעון, because it served as a base for the flame.

steps.title: רבי יהודה הנשיא allowed carrying a coal pan with its ashes
steps.stepSummary: A long chain of rabbis passes on רבי רומנוס's report: רבי allowed him to carry a coal pan together with its ashes on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said that רבי אסי said that רבי יוחנן said that רבי חנינא said that רבי רומנוס said: 'רבי permitted me to carry a coal pan with its ashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A statement is passed down through five rabbis: רבי יהודה הנשיא allowed carrying a coal pan full of ashes on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes left from burning have no use, so they are normally מוקצה. The surprise is that the pan may still be carried, even though it holds only forbidden ashes. Notice that רבי יוחנן is one of the links in the chain. The next step uses this to raise a question.

keyTerms.meaning: A coal pan, used for coals or for burning incense
Its ashes
To carry or move (on שבת)
Permitted

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Asi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yoḥanan said that Rabbi Ḥanina said
that Rabbi Romanus said:
Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) permitted me
to carry a coal pan with its ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִי הִתִּיר רַבִּי לְטַלְטֵל מַחְתָּה בְּאֶפְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about carrying a container that holds מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coal pan may be carried on שבת together with its ashes.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: רבי יוחנן allows the basket with a stone only because of the fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי how רבי יוחנן could report this. רבי יוחנן said a basket with a stone may be carried only when it also holds fruit. So a pan holding only ashes should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: 'Did רבי יוחנן really say this? We learned in a משנה: A person may pick up his son even if the son is holding a stone, or a basket with a stone inside it. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the משנה is talking about a basket full of fruit. So the reason it is allowed is that there is fruit in it. If there were no fruit, it would not be allowed!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the statement from step 2. He points out that רבי יוחנן ruled elsewhere in a way that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן explained that the basket with the stone may be carried only because of the fruit. The fruit is a permitted item, and the basket is carried for its sake. Without fruit, the basket would just be a base for the forbidden stone. The pan holds only ashes and nothing permitted, so by רבי יוחנן's own reasoning it should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say? A phrase that expresses doubt.
Basket
We are dealing with (this case)
'The reason is X, which means without X...' A pattern for drawing an inference from a ruling.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the משנה itself. It is about רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה (that the basket was full of fruit). That explanation suggests he would forbid a container holding only מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
Did Rabbi Yoḥanan really say this?
But didn't we learn: A person may pick up his son
while a stone is in his hand,
or a basket with a stone inside it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
We are dealing with a basket full of fruit.
The reason is that there is fruit in it;
but if there is no fruit in it — not allowed!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement from step 2 by pointing to a contradicting ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's report that a coal pan may be carried with its ashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן allows carrying a basket holding a stone only when it also holds fruit. So a container holding only מוקצה is forbidden, and the pan of ashes should be forbidden too.

steps.title: After a stunned silence, רבי אסי answers: the pan had bits of incense
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי is speechless for a moment. Then he answers that here too, the pan contained small leftover bits of incense, which are permitted items.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was stunned for a moment. Then he said: 'Here too, it is a case where the pan has small bits (of incense) in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי first has no answer. The גמרא uses a phrase from the book of דניאל to describe this. Then he answers by comparing the incense bits to the fruit in the basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי makes the pan case match the basket case. Unburned bits of incense are still usable, so they count as a permitted item, just like the fruit. The pan may then be carried for the sake of the incense, and the ashes go along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: He was stunned for a moment (from דניאל ד:טז). Used to describe someone who has no immediate answer.
Here too
Small bits or particles, here of incense that was not yet burned

phrases.english: "He was stunned for a moment" (Daniel 4:16),
and then he said: Here too
it is a case where it has small bits (of incense).

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר: הָכָא נָמֵי דְּאִית בַּהּ קְרָטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge by redefining the case of the pan.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the pan contained permitted items.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pan held only ashes, so it was a base for מוקצה alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pan also held usable bits of incense, just as the basket held fruit, so carrying it is permitted.

steps.title: אביי objects: tiny bits are worthless in רבי's wealthy house
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether tiny bits of incense would count as anything in the wealthy household of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Are tiny bits considered valuable in רבי's house?'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי אסי's answer. רבי was very wealthy, and no one in his home would treat leftover crumbs of incense as worth anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something only counts as a permitted item if it is valued. If the incense bits are worthless to their owner, they are just part of the ashes. Then the pan again holds nothing permitted, and the original question comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The household of רבי יהודה הנשיא, known for its great wealth
Considered significant or valuable

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: קְרָטִין בֵּי רַבִּי מִי חֲשִׁיבִי?
phrases.english: Abaye said: Are tiny bits considered significant in Rabbi's house?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אסי's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's claim that the incense bits make the pan permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Value depends on the owner. In רבי's rich household, the bits are worthless and simply become part of the ashes.

steps.title: The idea that the bits are useful to the poor is rejected
steps.stepSummary: אביי considers a defense: the bits are valuable to poor people. He rejects it using a ברייתא which teaches that something counts as valuable only according to the person who owns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if you say the bits are useful to poor people, we learned in a ברייתא: Clothing the size of poor people's garments counts for the poor, and clothing the size of rich people's garments counts for the rich. But poor people's clothing does not count for the rich.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises a possible way to save רבי אסי's answer and then knocks it down. The goal is to make his question from step 5 airtight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed defense: something useful to anyone, such as the poor, should count as valuable. The ברייתא, from the laws of טומאה of cloth, shows this is wrong. A small scrap counts for a poor owner but not for a rich one. So value is measured by the owner, and in רבי's house the bits remain worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. Introduces a possible defense that is about to be rejected.
They are fit (useful) for poor people
Poor people's clothing: small pieces of cloth that matter to a poor person

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about the size at which cloth can become טמא, not about מוקצה. The גמרא borrows only its principle: value is judged by the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule that comes up across the laws of מוקצה and טומאה: whether something counts as valuable can depend on who owns it.

phrases.english: And if you say: they are fit for poor people —
but it was taught: poor people's clothing counts for the poor,
rich people's clothing counts for the rich,
but poor people's clothing for the rich — does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to אביי's question, which strengthens it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed defense that the incense bits count as valuable because poor people could use them.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא shows that value is judged by the actual owner, not by what others might use it for.

steps.title: אביי's own answer: the pan is like a chamber pot of waste
steps.stepSummary: אביי sets aside the incense explanation. He says the ash pan is like a chamber pot of waste, which may be carried out because it is repulsive.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Rather, אביי said: It is just like the case of a chamber pot of waste.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the incense answer failed, אביי gives a completely different reason why carrying the pan is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even something with no use at all may be removed on שבת if it is disgusting to keep around, like a chamber pot of waste (גרף של רעי). A pan of ashes is also unpleasant to keep in the house. So it may be carried out, even though it holds only מוקצה. This explains רבי's permission without saying it contradicts רבי יוחנן's ruling about the basket.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Introduces a new answer that replaces the one that failed.
It is just like (the following case)
A chamber pot of waste. It may be removed on שבת because it is repulsive.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי suggests that the pan of ashes may be removed like a גרף של רעי, because repulsive things may be taken out on שבת. This is not the last word: in the next step רבא rejects the comparison, and in step 9 he gives his own reason.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It is just like a chamber pot of waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַגְּרָף שֶׁל רֶיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי אסי's rejected answer with a new reason for permitting the pan.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new legal category: removing something repulsive (גרף של רעי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pan could be permitted only if it held something valuable, such as incense bits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pan may be carried because ashes are repulsive, like a chamber pot, even with nothing valuable in it.

steps.title: רבא rejects the chamber pot comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives two reasons why the ash pan cannot be compared to a גרף של רעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are two answers against this. One, a chamber pot of waste is disgusting, and this ash pan is not disgusting. Also, a chamber pot is uncovered, and this ash pan is covered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down אביי's answer from step 7, which compared the ash pan to a chamber pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גרף של רעי may be carried only because it is repulsive and must be removed. An ash pan is not repulsive. It is also covered, so it does not bother anyone, and the reason for removing it does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Two refutations or answers against a claim
A chamber pot holding waste
Repulsive or disgusting
Uncovered / covered

phrases.english: Rava said: There are two refutations of this matter:
One, a chamber pot of waste is repulsive,
and this (ash pan) is not repulsive.
And furthermore, a chamber pot of waste is uncovered,
and this one is covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's chamber-pot answer from step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole comparison between the ash pan and a גרף של רעי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ash pan has neither feature that permits moving a chamber pot: it is not disgusting and it is not exposed

steps.title: רבא: the pan may be moved because of the ashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that at רב נחמן's house they carried a coal pan for the sake of its ashes, even when broken wood was on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: When we were at the house of רב נחמן, we used to carry the coal pan because of the ashes, even though there were broken pieces of wood on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own explanation for why the pan may be moved: the ashes themselves are a useful, permitted item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes can be used, for example to cover dirt, so they are not מוקצה. The pan may therefore be carried as a holder of something permitted. The useless broken wood counts as secondary to the ashes and does not make the pan forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A coal pan or fire pan
On account of, as part of
Ashes
Broken pieces of wood

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
When we were at the house of Rav Nachman,
we would move the coal pan on account of the ashes,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ שִׁבְרֵי עֵצִים.
phrases.english: even though there were broken pieces of wood on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected explanation with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason: the ashes are themselves a permitted, useful item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A pan holding only ashes is like a basket with only a stone, so it is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: The ashes are useful, so the pan may be moved for them, and broken wood on it is secondary

steps.title: Challenge from wick fragments in a lamp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a lamp with wick fragments in it may not be moved. So small useless items should not be cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: "And they agree that if there are fragments of wick in it, it is forbidden to move it!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's claim that the broken wood is cancelled out by the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the lamp holds oil, which is a usable item, yet a few wick fragments still make it forbidden to move. This suggests that small מוקצה items are not cancelled out by a permitted item. That contradicts רבא's report about the broken wood.

keyTerms.meaning: And they (the disputing תנאים) agree
Fragments of a wick

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ שִׁבְרֵי פְּתִילָה
phrases.english: And they agree that if there are fragments of wick in it,
that it is forbidden to move it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the final clause of רבא's statement, about the broken wood
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that broken wood is cancelled out by the ashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wick fragments are not cancelled out by the oil, broken wood should not be cancelled out by ashes either

steps.title: אביי: that ruling was taught in the גליל
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא reflects conditions in the גליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They taught that ruling in the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to a particular place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב ניסים גאון, oil was plentiful and cheap in the גליל. The oil there is not important enough to cancel out the wick fragments. Ashes in a normal place are valued enough to cancel out broken wood.

keyTerms.meaning: The Galil, the northern region of ארץ ישראל, rich in oil
They taught

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a small forbidden item is cancelled out depends on how important the permitted item is in that place.

phrases.english: Abaye said: They taught it in the Galilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the wick fragments
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a local case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Small useless items are never cancelled out
steps.terutzMaskana: In the גליל cheap oil cannot cancel out the wicks, but ashes elsewhere can cancel out wood

steps.title: לוי בר שמואל asks about reassembling a weaver's frame
steps.stepSummary: לוי בר שמואל asks רבי אבא and רב הונא בר חייא whether one may reassemble a weaver's frame on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי בר שמואל found רבי אבא and רב הונא בר חייא standing at the doorway of רב הונא's house. He asked them: What is the law about reassembling a weaver's frame on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a story. The גמרא is setting up a question about putting a take-apart frame back together on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מטה של טרסיים was a frame that could be taken apart. The question is whether putting it back together counts as building or finishing a utensil, which would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He found them
Doorway or entrance
To put back, to reassemble
A weaver's frame that can be taken apart

phrases.english: Levi bar Shmuel found

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי אַבָּא וּלְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba and Rav Huna bar Chiya,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲווֹ קָיְימִי אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי רַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: who were standing at the doorway of Rav Huna's house.
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְהַחֲזִיר מִטָּה שֶׁל טַרְסִיִּים בְּשַׁבָּת?
phrases.english: What is the law about reassembling a weaver's frame on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ לְהַחֲזִיר מִטָּה שֶׁל טַרְסִיִּים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, reassembling utensils on שבת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether reassembling a take-apart weaver's frame is permitted on שבת

steps.title: They answer that it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא and רב הונא בר חייא say it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The two rabbis give a lenient answer: one may reassemble the frame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They hold that putting this frame back together is not a forbidden act at all. This answer is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, permitted

phrases.english: They said to him: It is fine.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reassembling the weaver's frame is permitted

steps.title: רב יהודה: רב and שמואל say one is liable to a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב ושמואל that reassembling a weaver's frame on שבת makes one liable to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב יהודה. רב יהודה said: But רב and שמואל both said that one who reassembles a weaver's frame on שבת is liable to bring a חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: לוי בר שמואל brings the same question to רב יהודה, who gives the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for a חטאת means this is a full Torah-level מלאכה, not merely a rabbinic restriction. That is the extreme opposite of "it is fine".

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Liable to bring a sin-offering, meaning a Torah violation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the people. לוי בר שמואל only asked the question. The lenient ruling came from רבי אבא and רב הונא בר חייא, and they are the ones challenged next.

phrases.english: He came before Rav Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הָא רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: he said: But Rav and Shmuel both said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּחֲזִיר מִטָּה שֶׁל טַרְסִיִּים בְּשַׁבָּת — חַיָּיב חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: One who reassembles a weaver's frame on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the lenient answer of step 13
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the ruling of רב ושמואל that this is a Torah violation

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא about reassembling objects
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that reassembling objects is liable or at least forbidden. That contradicts the ruling that it is "fine".
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who puts back a branch of a מנורה on שבת is liable to a חטאת. A plasterer's pole should not be put back, and if he did put it back, he is exempt but it is forbidden. רבי סימאי says: For a curved horn he is liable, and for a straight horn he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא and רב הונא בר חייא using a ברייתא about reassembling objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case in this ברייתא, reassembling is either a Torah violation (חייב) or at least forbidden (פטור אבל אסור). None of the cases is fully permitted, so how could anyone say "שפיר דמי"?

keyTerms.meaning: A branch of a candelabrum
A plasterer's pole made of parts
Exempt from punishment but still forbidden
A curved horn (hard to assemble) / a straight horn (easy to assemble)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּחֲזִיר קְנֵה מְנוֹרָה בְּשַׁבָּת — חַיָּיב חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: One who reattaches a branch of a candelabrum on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering.
A plasterer's pole: one should not reassemble it,
and if he reassembled it, he is exempt, but it is forbidden.
Rabbi Simai says:
A curved horn: he is liable.
A straight horn: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's view and attacks the lenient answer from a תנאי source
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling "שפיר דמי" of רבי אבא and רב הונא בר חייא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא never fully permits reassembling. At best it is פטור אבל אסור, so a full permit contradicts it.

steps.title: The lenient rabbis follow a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the lenient rabbis follow another ברייתא, which begins with bed frames, bed legs, and archer's tablets.
steps.simpleTranslation: They ruled like this תנא, as it was taught: The frame of a bed, the legs of a bed, and the tablets of a bow should not be put back. If he did put them back, he is exempt...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: the lenient rabbis follow a different תנא. Here the גמרא starts quoting his ברייתא, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the quoted part says "exempt" (פטור), but not yet fully permitted. The ruling that supports "שפיר דמי" comes later in this ברייתא, on the next עמוד. For now, the learner should know that the answer is "they follow another תנא".

keyTerms.meaning: They ruled according to this תנא
The wooden frame of a bed
The legs of a bed
The tablets of a bow (archer's tablets)

phrases.english: They ruled in accordance with this Tanna,
as it was taught (in a baraita):
The frame of a bed and the legs of a bed
and the tablets of a bow: one should not put them back,
and if he put them back, he is exempt,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Disputed among תנאים: the lenient rabbis follow a different תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a תנא whose view supports the lenient ruling, and his full position is completed on the next עמוד
